foreignConfig.notice: config.txt has {{count}} other active filter line(s) that stack on top of every CAGEq correction.
foreignConfig.reviewBody: These active lines in Equalizer APO's config.txt apply on top of every CAGEq correction — usually the default preamp / example filters from a fresh install. Comment them out so only your CAGEq correction is applied? Nothing is deleted — they're marked and can be restored.
foreignConfig.doneBody: Those lines are commented out, so only CAGEq's correction applies now. They're kept in config.txt with a CAGEq marker and can be restored.

selfTest.buttonTitle: Play a test signal and verify your correction actually reaches the output
selfTest.warnBody: This plays a short burst of pink noise through {{device}}. Turn your volume DOWN first and stop any other audio.
selfTest.running: Testing… measuring the loopback with your correction and bypassed (a few seconds; the sound will briefly change).
selfTest.rawNote: Raw loopback spectrum shown during the test — watch it flatten when the correction is bypassed.
selfTest.pass: The measured output matches your correction (shape match {{r}}%). Equalizer APO is applying it.
selfTest.failTitle: ✕ No EQ detected at the output
selfTest.fail:
The output didn't change with your correction — Equalizer APO isn't affecting this device. Check:
• Audio enhancements are enabled for the device (Windows Sound → device → Properties).
• Equalizer APO is installed on it (run its DeviceSelector).
• No other filters in config.txt are interfering.
selfTest.mismatch: Something is shaping the output, but not the way your correction predicts (match {{r}}%). Other active filters in config.txt may be stacking on top.
selfTest.nosignal: The loopback captured almost nothing, so there's nothing to compare — the output device was likely disabled or removed. Check it's active, then retry. (The device's own volume/mute don't affect this test; only muting CAGEq itself in the Windows volume mixer would.)
selfTest.inconclusive: Your current correction is too flat to test reliably. Pick a headphone correction with more shape (Slot A or B), then retry.
selfTest.deviceColor: ⚠ The Dry signal isn't flat (±{{db}} dB) — the output device seems to apply its own processing (audio enhancements, spatial sound, a fixed EQ). Disable those for a truthful correction and A/B.
